question: Whether the RMSNorm Qwen3.5 runs on this stack gives a row the same result regardless of how many rows share its batch. The cross-card all-reduce was ruled out as the sole cause of the two-card identity loss (campaigns r0/r1), and the Flash-Next lane's precedent was that a norm was the second shape-dependent reduction.
method: The op is instantiated directly inside a vLLM config context and fed the same rows alone and batched; outputs are compared bitwise. No server and no second card. float16, the model's serving dtype. The forward actually dispatched is forward_native, which matches what the server selects (IrOpPriorityConfig(rms_norm=['native'])); it lowers to ir.ops.rms_norm.
finding: Row-count dependent. A row's output can differ from the same row computed alone, at roughly 2-3% of rows once the batch reaches 16, and never below 8 in this sample. Differences are last-bit float16.
sampling_note: An early single-seed run appeared to show a clean threshold at 32 rows. It does not hold: other seeds show differences at 16 and none at 32. The effect is stochastic and data-dependent, so the table above aggregates ten seeds per row count rather than reporting one draw.
input_caveat: Inputs are standard normal, not real activations. The rate on real hidden states may differ; what is established is that the dependence exists on the serving path, not its exact frequency in production.
why_it_matters: It supplies the residue the all-reduce experiment could not remove, and it fits the observed identity behaviour: ladders are exact at low concurrency, where the norm is invariant, and lose occasional requests from 16 users up, where a small fraction of rows carry a last-bit perturbation that only changes a token when it coincides with a near-tie. It also explains why the one-card W4A16 route can be exact at 64 users and still miss one request at 96: the perturbation rate is roughly flat while whether it matters is a matter of ties.
scope: This does not show the norm causes any specific observed miss, and it does not make the GEMM story wrong. It shows the lab has been treating row-invariance as a property of the matmul when a second op on the same path does not have it.
